title: Post-translational modification patterns on beta-myosin heavy chain are altered in ischemic and nonischemic human hearts.
authors: Landim-Vieira, Maicon; Childers, Matthew C; Wacker, Amanda L; Garcia, Michelle Rodriquez; He, Huan; Singh, Rakesh; Brundage, Elizabeth A; Johnston, Jamie R; Whitson, Bryan A; Chase, P Bryant; Janssen, Paul M L; Regnier, Michael; Biesiadecki, Brandon J; Pinto, J Renato; Parvatiyar, Michelle S
one_liner_zh: 该文通过蛋白质组学鉴定心肌β-肌球蛋白重链的翻译后修饰，并用MD模拟探究其对蛋白-DNA互作无关的肌丝结构影响，虽涉及MD方法但对象非蛋白质-DNA互作，仅部分可借鉴其模拟思路。
abstract: Phosphorylation and acetylation of sarcomeric proteins are important for fine-tuning myocardial contractility. Here, we used bottom-up proteomics and label-free quantification to identify novel post-translational modifications (PTMs) on beta-myosin heavy chain (beta-MHC) in normal and failing human heart tissues. We report six acetylated lysines and two phosphorylated residues: K34-Ac, K58-Ac, S210-P, K213-Ac, T215-P, K429-Ac, K951-Ac, and K1195-Ac. K951-Ac was significantly reduced in both ischemic and nonischemic failing hearts compared to nondiseased hearts. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations show that K951-Ac may impact stability of thick filament tail interactions and ultimately myosin head positioning. K58-Ac altered the solvent-exposed SH3 domain surface - known for protein-protein interactions - but did not appreciably change motor domain conformation or dynamics under conditions studied. Together, K213-Ac/T215-P altered loop 1's structure and dynamics - known to regulate ADP-release, ATPase activity, and sliding velocity. Our study suggests that beta-MHC acetylation levels may be influenced more by the PTM location than the type of heart disease since less protected acetylation sites are reduced in both heart failure groups. Additionally, these PTMs have potential to modulate interactions between beta-MHC and other regulatory sarcomeric proteins, ADP-release rate of myosin, flexibility of the S2 region, and cardiac myofilament contractility in normal and failing hearts.
abstract_zh: 肌节蛋白的磷酸化和乙酰化对于精细调节心肌收缩性至关重要。在此，我们采用自下而上的蛋白质组学和无标记定量方法，在正常和衰竭人类心脏组织中鉴定了β-肌球蛋白重链（beta-MHC）上的新型翻译后修饰（PTMs）。我们报告了六个乙酰化赖氨酸和两个磷酸化残基：K34-Ac、K58-Ac、S210-P、K213-Ac、T215-P、K429-Ac、K951-Ac和K1195-Ac。与无疾病心脏相比，缺血性和非缺血性衰竭心脏中K951-Ac显著减少。分子动力学（MD）模拟显示，K951-Ac可能影响粗丝尾部相互作用的稳定性，并最终影响肌球蛋白头部定位。K58-Ac改变了暴露于溶剂的SH3结构域表面——已知该区域参与蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用——但在所研究的条件下并未显著改变运动结构域的构象或动力学。此外，K213-Ac/T215-P改变了环1的结构和动力学——已知该区域调节ADP释放、ATP酶活性和滑动速度。我们的研究表明，beta-MHC乙酰化水平可能更多受PTM位置而非心脏病类型的影响，因为在两种心力衰竭组中，保护较少的乙酰化位点均减少。此外，这些PTMs具有调节beta-MHC与其他调节性肌节蛋白之间相互作用、肌球蛋白ADP释放速率、S2区域灵活性以及正常和衰竭心脏中心肌肌丝收缩性的潜力。
